article_sentences: “The Odisha government on Friday (October 30, 2026) intensified rescue-and-relief operations, deploying four defence helicopters to airdrop food packets in flood-hit Ganjam district, where thousands of people remain marooned for more than 24 hours following heavy rainfall triggered by cyclone Arnab,” officials said.

Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh P. Patil said four helicopters had begun dropping food packets at 21 identified locations in the district, with personnel stationed there tasked with distributing them among stranded people.

“Helicopters of the Indian Navy and Indian Coast Guard are engaged in the operation, covering areas including Hinjilicut, Purushottampur, Seragada, Dharakote, Aska, Belaguntha, Bhanjanagar and Chikiti, where several areas remain cut off due to flooding,” officials said.

"The packets carry as much as 4,500 kg of grains, which will be dropped at one place and officials stationed there will later distribute them among the affected people," Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said.
“Other affected people are being provided cooked food by rescue teams, which are transporting supplies in boats,” he said.
Mr. Pujari said more than 23,000 people were staying in relief camps, but the number of those marooned was considerably higher.
He said 40 trained personnel of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) would reach affected areas with cooked food to assist stranded people.
“Movement of boats to several locations had earlier been difficult due to strong water currents, but the situation had improved slightly on Friday (October 30, 2026),” he said.
“Of the 313 rescue teams deployed across the State, more than 100 are engaged in Ganjam and Gajapati districts,” the Minister said.
“A central team will visit the State on November 2 to assess the damage caused by floods triggered by cyclone Arnab,” he added.
“Ganjam is the worst-affected district, while Gajapati and Kandhamal have also suffered damage.
The government has not received any report of casualties so far,” Mr. Pujari said.

stories.headline: Netanyahu's Likud Bloc wins 53 seats in Israel election
stories.title: Netanyahu's Likud Bloc wins 53 seats in Israel election
stories.summary: Jerusalem, Oct 30 : Israel’s 2026 election results left no political bloc with a parliamentary majority in the 26th Knesset, as the Central Elections Committee (CEC) released the final results on Friday morning, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud-led bloc winning 53 seats, the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party securing 48, and Arab factions accounting for the remaining 19 seats. The outcome marked a significant decline in Netanyahu’s coalition, whose constituent parties held 68 seats in the outgoing Knesset, The Times of Israel reported. The official results are scheduled to be submitted to Israeli President Isaac Herzog on November 4, following the CEC’s completion of final checks into any reported errors or complaints. Herzog will subsequently hold consultations with each party leader, who will recommend their preferred candidate to form the next government. Despite the uncertainty surrounding government formation, the newly elected Knesset is set to be sworn in on November 10. Reports suggest that efforts to form the next government are expected to be challenging and could extend beyond two months, with neither political camp close to securing the 61 seats required for a parliamentary majority. The final voter turnout was 77.9 per cent of eligible voters, the highest figure in decades On Wednesday, Herzog called on political leaders to make every effort to prevent another election, urging those involved in government formation talks to approach the process with an open mind. “We must do everything we can, certainly after yesterday, to avoid another round of elections. So I expect everyone who comes here to come with an open mind,” The Times of Israel quoted Herzog as saying. Both Netanyahu and Eisenkot have maintained that they would be the ones to form the next government. Earlier this week, addressing supporters at the Likud election headquarters in Jerusalem after the polls, Netanyahu asserted that the right wing commanded a “great majority” among Israel’s “Zionist public” and called for the formation of a “strong right-wing government”. He also criticised parties willing to cooperate with Arab parties, calling such an arrangement a “shame”. The Tuesday elections marked the first electoral contest since the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack, amid significant shifts in the political landscape and the issues shaping voter priorities since the 2022 elections. --IANS

article_sentences: The enquiry will be led by the District Magistrate (North-East), said the official in a statement, adding that it will also check for lapses on the part of government agencies and officials and fix responsibility.

New Delhi: Delhi Home and Urban Development Minister, Ashish Sood, has ordered a magisterial enquiry into a building collapse in New Seemapuri that claimed four lives earlier this month, an official said on Friday.
Sood said, "This is a deeply tragic incident that has cost precious lives.
We have ordered a magisterial enquiry to investigate every single aspect of this collapse.
No guilty person or lax official will be spared.”
“Our immediate priority is to support the affected families, and our long-term goal is to enforce strict structural safety rules so that such an accident never happens again in Delhi," he said.
A five-storey residential building (House No. E-402, built on a small plot of 20-25 square yards) collapsed on October 7 around 3 p.m. in New Seemapuri, Delhi.
Three adjacent structures suffered major damage, were declared unsafe by the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), and were evacuated.
Initial local enquiries indicate that demolition work using heavy, vibration-causing machinery on an adjacent unauthorised construction site triggered the collapse.
Nearby residential structures in the area have also been found to be weak buildings constructed on tiny plots without proper structural columns or beams.
Sood said the magisterial enquiry into the collapse has the mandate to ascertain the exact facts, circumstances, and root causes of the building collapse.

It will also identify violations of laws, building rules, and safety stipulations by owners, tenants, or private individuals and also check for lapses or omissions on the part of government departments, civic agencies, and their officers to fix accountability.

stories.headline: Why the IDBI Bank sale matters beyond Rs52,878 crore price tag
stories.title: Why the IDBI Bank sale matters beyond Rs52,878 crore price tag
stories.summary: As the long-delayed sale of IDBI Bank comes to a close, the significance of the ₹52,878 crore transaction extends far beyond the cheque that Fairfax is set to write. The deal marks the government’s most consequential strategic disinvestment since Air India in 2022. It also offers a rare example of a complex privatisation reaching fruition after years of regulatory, operational and investor-related hurdles.On October 14, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the sale of IDBI Bank to Canada-based Fairfax Financial Holding. According to the deal contour, Fairfax Financial Holdings will get 60.72 percent stake in IDBI Bank for ₹52,878 crore. Of the total sale, the government will sell 30.48 percent and retain 15 percent, while the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) will sell 30.24 percent and keep 19 percent. The government’s share of the proceeds is expected to be about ₹26,000 crore.The IDBI deal with Fairfax delivers the government’s most significant strategic disinvestment since Air India and provides a much-needed boost to FY27 divestment receipts. More importantly, it signals that large-scale state-owned assets can still attract long-term capital, providing fresh momentum to India’s privatisation agenda at a time when the government’s disinvestment programme has struggled to meet its targets.Also Read: Markets fund 74% of Centre’s disinvestment; strategic sales under 10%However, the transaction also lays bare a persistent weakness in India’s privatisation plan. The government’s disinvestment programme remains heavily reliant on a handful of marquee transactions to meet ambitious asset-sale targets, raising questions about the depth and sustainability of the broader privatisation pipeline.“The IDBI sale shows India’s privatisation programme can deliver, but slowly, case by case, and with the state keeping a minority foothold rather than leaving outright. The IDBI stake sale can become a template where a foreign buyer can control an Indian bank. It also emboldens the government’s strategic sale privatisation programme, especially in public sector banks,” says Garima Kapoor, deputy head of research and economist-institutional equities, Elara Securities.For market observers, the IDBI Bank sale is significant not only because of its size but also because it offers a potential blueprint for future strategic sales. The structure balances private-sector control with continued government participation, a model that could make privatisation financially more palatable.According to Manish Aggarwal, partner and leader, financial services and infrastructure transactions, Deloitte India, it is one of the largest and most complex strategic disinvestments undertaken by the government. The IDBI Bank deal marks a significant milestone in India’s reform journey, advances the government’s disinvestment objectives and reinforces the country’s position as an attractive destination for long-term foreign investment, according to him.“The deal is structured very well… the foreign investor gets management control, brings in capital, expertise to grow the bank, and the government rides this upside through its residual stake. With global investors continuing to back India’s growth potential with the largest foreign direct investment in the sector despite an uncertain geopolitical environment is testimony to India’s political stability, continued focus on reforms and belief in the highest growth rates of our economy,” says Aggarwal. He adds the deal is also an important step in attracting long-term foreign capital into a sector that will play a critical role in supporting India’s next phase of growth.Analysts at Choice Institutional Equities agree: “Closing a sale that has dragged on for years is a genuine win.”However, it also exposes the privatisation programme’s continued dependence on infrequent, big-ticket strategic sales. The analysts explain that one transaction delivering roughly a third of the full-year target underscores how thin and lumpy the disinvestment pipeline remains. “Leaning on a single large ticket to rescue the FY27 number looks like a familiar pattern rather than a structural fix. The terms are also accommodating to the buyer, with a 15-year runway to pare the stake and two years to resolve the CSB Bank overlap. Execution risk now shifts to regulatory clearances and completion timing, and budget math that leans on one closing stays fragile,” they say. In 2018, Fairfax had acquired 51 percent in CSB Bank (earlier known as Catholic Syrian Bank). Currently, it holds 40 percent in CSB Bank.According to the terms of the deal, Fairfax must cut its holding to 26 percent over 15 years and exit or merge its 40 percent stake in CSB Bank within two years. The government plans to divest its remaining 15 percent stake in IDBI Bank through market sale, while LIC will manage its residual holding, paving the way for a gradual transition to private ownership.Also Read: Fairfax to buy 60.7% of IDBI Bank for Rs52,878 crore in biggest banking FDIRoad to privatisationThe IDBI stake sale is expected to fill up the government’s coffers and the divestment target for this fiscal is likely to be met for the first time in eight years. In the first five months (April-August) of FY27, the government had achieved nearly 70 percent of its annual divestment target, raising about ₹55,700 crore, before accounting for the IDBI Bank stake sale. The contrast with recent years is striking. Between FY20 and FY26, the government had hit, on average, just 33 percent of its budgeted disinvestment targets, reflecting persistent challenges in executing strategic sales and a reliance on stake dilutions and buybacks to bridge the gap.Kapoor says the share sale in IDBI Bank is expected to lift FY27 disinvestment proceeds to ₹82,301 crore, above the ₹80,000 crore target, offering critical buffer at a time when government finances are facing stress due to higher subsidies and excise duty cuts on petrol and diesel. In May, the government approved the strategic sale of Indian Medicines Pharmaceutical Corporation to Delhi-based pharma manufacturer Skymap Pharmaceuticals Private for ₹121.01 crore.Proceeds from the sale of 6.5 percent in LIC (₹31,500 crore) form a large chunk of the disinvestment in the current fiscal. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) had granted LIC a three-year extension in May 2024 to achieve the 10 percent free float target. By launching the offer-for-sale in August, the government met the mandated threshold nine months ahead of the deadline.India’s privatisation push gained momentum with the sale of Air India in 2022, and the government’s broader strategy of reducing its presence in non-strategic sectors. However, execution has lagged ambition. Several proposed strategic sales, including BPCL and Shipping Corporation of India, have faced delays because of regulatory, legal and market-related hurdles.As a result, the government has frequently fallen short of its divestment targets. It has relied more on minority stake sales and buybacks by public sector companies than outright privatisation. Against this backdrop, the IDBI Bank transaction stands out.Also Read: IDBI Bank divestment: Strong optics and no hidden surprises lure potential buyersWhat’s in it for Fairfax?For Fairfax, the ₹81-per-share offer provides a pathway to acquire a banking franchise at a valuation that meets the government’s sale criteria while securing management control of one of India’s larger lenders. “Since the winning best offer bid of ₹81 per share was above the benchmark price, as well as fair value estimates of both the independent valuation agencies, it was adjudged to be reasonable and approved,” says a government statement to the stock exchanges.However, the valuation could not win market investors’ confidence. The ₹81-per share was lower than the closing price of ₹90.16 on October 14 when the deal was announced. Since then, investors are dumping shares of IDBI Bank in the secondary markets. The stock is down 14 percent in less than 10 days, indicating investor concerns over the takeover valuations.For Fairfax, the acquisition is a long-term vision than just a strategic buy. “Fairfax’s objective in buying the 60.72 percent interest in IDBI Bank is to make it, over time, a leading global Indian bank headquartered in India,” according to a company statement.Fairfax’s bet extends beyond banking. It is still awaiting approval from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and needs to comply with prescribed regulatory conditions to complete the IDBI Bank deal. However, the Prem Watsa-led company has chalked out its long-term plan for the combined entity. It wants to create a platform to build a diversified financial services franchise spanning insurance, wealth management and investment banking, while capitalising on India’s long-term credit expansion and financialisation.Fairfax plans to combine all its stakes in Digit (Go Digit Life Insurance and Go Digit General Insurance) and IIFL Capital Services to IDBI Bank. Fairfax owns a 30.2 percent stake in IIFL Capital Services and 49 percent stake in Digit.“Combining IDBI Bank, Digit and IIFL Capital would create an entity that is well-positioned to participate in the continued growth and success of Indian markets, and we expect it to provide meaningful and significant benefits to Indian consumers and businesses, as well as to IDBI Bank, Digit, IIFL Capital and to Fairfax for many decades to come,” says Prem Watsa, chairman and CEO, Fairfax, in a statement.Watsa feels that a newly revitalised IDBI Bank that can also offer clients insurance products through Digit, and investment banking and wealth management services through IIFL Capital would be in a competitive position to take advantage of India’s growth.Following the IDBI transaction, Fairfax expects the operations of the combined company to be led by Rakesh Sharma, managing director and CEO of the bank. It also plans to include in the IDBI Bank’s leadership group CVR Rajendran, former CEO of CSB Bank, as well as NS Kannan, former MD and CEO of ICICI Prudential Life Company, and CFO of ICICI Bank, who will act as chairman. All this is subject to approval from the RBI, says a company statement.Fairfax does not expect any change in the governance, management or operating structure of either Digit or IIFL Capital due to the merged entity.Post the stake sale announcement, Crisil has placed its rating on the long-term debt instruments of IDBI Bank on ‘rating watch with positive implications’ and has reaffirmed its ‘Crisil A1+’ rating on the certificate of deposit programme. The ratings agency believes that IDBI Bank is likely to benefit from Fairfax’s majority ownership and strategic commitment.“Over the past few years, IDBI Bank has demonstrated a sustained improvement in its standalone credit profile, reflected in improved asset quality, healthy profitability and comfortable capitalisation profile. The proposed acquisition has the potential to further strengthen the bank’s business profile by providing access to Fairfax’s broader financial services ecosystem, including insurance and wealth management businesses,” Crisil says.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court recently reserved judgment on the issue whether the period spent to acquire Ph.D. can be counted towards teaching experience for the appointment as Associate Professor as per the norms of the University Grants Commission.

A bench comprising Justice Sanjay Kumar and Justice Manmohan heard the petitions filed by the UGC as well as Professor Joseph Skaria challenging the Kerala High Court's 2023 judgment which upheld the appointment of Priya Varghese, wife of CPI(M) KK Ragesh who was the Private Secretary to the then Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, in the Kannur University.

The issue arose after Dr.Joseph Skariah, who was ranked after Varghese in the Rank List, had filed the writ petition challenging the inclusion of Varghese in the List, stating that she was not qualified for the post of Associate Professor as she did not have the prescribed 8 years of teaching experience.
A single judge of the Kerala High Court found that Varghese didn't have the requisite teaching experience and directed Kannur University to re-examine her credentials.
This was challenged by Varghese before the division bench, which held it in her favour.
Against this, the aggrieved candidate and the UGC appealed to the Supreme Court.
"The time taken by candidates to acquire M.Phil.
and/or Ph.D. Degree shall not be considered as teaching/research experience to be claimed for appointment to the teaching positions.

Further, the period of active service spent on pursuing a Research Degree simultaneously with teaching assignment without taking any kind of leave, shall be counted as teaching experience for the purpose of direct recruitment/promotion.

Regular faculty members up to twenty percent of the total faculty strength (excluding faculty on medical/maternity leave) shall be allowed by their respective institutions to take study leave for pursuing Ph.D. degree."
He submitted that Regulation 3.1.1 is divided into three parts; the first is a general provision applying to all "candidates".
Whereas the second part extends to those in active service, and the third part is merely a guideline for regular faculty.

stories.title: Asian Paints’ strokes of price hikes to fight inflation yet to brighten margins
stories.summary: Asian Paints has raised prices and is banking on sourcing efficiencies and its new VAE facility to offset input cost inflation, but competition could limit margin recovery.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Asian Paints’ consolidated gross margin felt the heat of high-cost inventory absorption in the September quarter (Q2FY27), sliding to a 15-quarter low of 39.7%, down around 350 basis points (bps) year-on-year.
The cost of goods sold rose 24% year-on-year last quarter.
Since this pressure was already anticipated, Asian Paints took a 5% price hike in Q2, following the 7% increase in Q1.
The raw material inflation scenario remains uncertain, so a further price increase of 3.5% has been announced for November.
This also factors in the anti-dumping duty on key input titanium dioxide (TiO2).
Asian Paints estimates a cost impact of 2-3% from the duty, which it is mitigating by rationalizing TiO2 use through alternative chemistries.
Dealer channel checks by Systematix Shares and Stocks (India) indicate that Asian Paints will take another price hike of 3-4%, effective 21 November, likely across product categories.
This would take the cumulative hikes since April to 19-20%.
Asian Paints has said price hikes will remain calibrated as it wants to avoid disrupting consumer demand amid elevated competition.
Aggressive cost pass-through could lead to downtrading, given the discretionary nature of paints, eventually hurting market share.
Besides price actions, Asian Paints is also banking on sourcing efficiencies and cost optimization to protect profitability.
It has guided for a gross margin band of 41-43% and expects to maintain an Ebitda margin of 18-20% for FY27, aided by premiumization.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court has directed Atibir Industries Co.

to pay an additional ₹125 crore to an asset reconstruction company (ARC) to achieve a full and final settlement of its loan dispute with the State Bank of India (SBI), while leaving open the legal questions concerning the classification of its loan account as a non-performing asset (NPA) and the subsequent assignment of the debt.

A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana passed the order in appeals challenging a Calcutta High Court Division Bench judgment that had reversed a Single Judge's decision setting aside SBI's NPA classification and consequential assignment-related actions.

“…in the peculiar circumstances of the case without going into any legal issues or whether the compensation amount will have to be calculated on the basis of the debt value or the acquisition value etc. and without expressing any opinion on the conduct of the parties, this Court directs that a sum of Rs.125 crores over and above a sum of Rs.250 crores will have to be paid by the Appellant to the Respondent No.2… This will be towards the full and final settlement of the entire dues payable by the Appellant towards the debt assigned by the Respondent No.1 in favour of the Respondent No.2.

This amount has been fixed without going into the issue whether it is a return on investment or otherwise so as to bring an end to the dispute which is continued between the parties for years.”, the Court ordered.
The Appellant, Atibir Industries, had availed credit facilities from a consortium of banks led by SBI.
SBI classified its loan account as an NPA with effect from October 16, 2020, and subsequently assigned the debt to the ARC on March 24, 2023, for ₹250 crores.

The company challenged the NPA classification, contending that it was premature in view of the Reserve Bank of India's COVID-19-related moratorium measures, which extended the repayment moratorium until August 31, 2020.
It also questioned the validity of the debt assignment.
The Calcutta High Court's Single Judge accepted the challenge and set aside the NPA classification and consequential actions.
However, the Division Bench reversed that decision.

Before the Supreme Court, the parties' submissions primarily focused on the report submitted by Justice Dave and whether the ARC was entitled to receive any amount beyond the ₹250 crore already paid by Atibir Industries.

article_sentences: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Friday said that the Delhi High Court takes a "disproportionate burden" off the Supreme Court as compared to other High Courts.

CJI said that the top court often reminds lawyers appearing before it that the Delhi High Court is "just around the corner" and that relief may be available there before their matters reach the Supreme Court.
The CJI was addressing a function organised to mark the Diamond Jubilee celebrations of the Delhi High Court, which completed 60 years.
The function was held in the Delhi High Court auditorium in S Block.

The CJI said that the High Court's location in the national capital places upon it a responsibility of extraordinary magnitude, as matters concerning governmental authority, individual liberty and public accountability regularly reach its courtrooms.
He said that the responsibilities of the Delhi High Court have multiplied with the expansion of the city, growth in commerce and increase in litigation over the years.
"What began as a court of just four judges is today an institution that resolves disputes of remarkable variety and complexity.
This High Court deserves every appreciation for rising to those demands," he said.
The CJI also highlighted the Delhi High Court's contribution to civil and commercial jurisprudence, particularly its role in developing alternative dispute resolution mechanisms.
He noted that the High Court established India's first High Court-annexed arbitration centre in 2009.

He further highlighted its original civil jurisdiction, which allows significant civil and commercial disputes to be heard directly by the High Court without litigants having to approach district courts first.
The CJI also praised the High Court's specialised Intellectual Property Division, saying that it has earned a formidable reputation in India and abroad for the quality of its jurisprudence.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court today called on the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology to include in its proposed policy a provision for action against the breach of the Court's directions restraining unauthorised uploading of audio-video clips of court proceedings.

On the last date, the Court instructed its Registry to forward the suggestions received by the Court to the office of the Solicitor General.

Justice Bagchi emphasised that difficulty persisted in implementation.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court upheld the conviction of a former Sub-Registrar under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (PC Act) for possessing assets disproportionate to his known sources of income.

It also held that once the prosecution establishes the disproportion with reference to known sources of income, the burden squarely rests on the accused to show that the assets were acquired from lawful sources.
A bench of Justice Sanjay Kumar and Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva held so while dismissing the appeal filed by the accused (appellant) against the Kerala High Court's 2025 judgment.
The accused who was on interim bail, has been granted two weeks to surrender before the trial court to undergo the remaining sentence.
The appellant joined as a Lower Division Clerk (LDC) in 1971 and became a Sub Registrar in 1993.
As per the prosecution, he acquired assets by illegal means between 1993 and 2001 that were disproportionate to his known sources of income.
The assets possessed by him and his family were worth Rs 1,93,898 at the start of the check period and Rs 12,37,720 at its end.
During this period, they earned Rs 10,12,117.20 and incurred expenditure of Rs 4,93,424, leaving Rs 5,18,693 as the amount (likely savings) which the appellant could not explain.
Subsequently, an FIR was registered in 2001 under Section 13(1)(e) read with Section 13(2) of the PC Act.
After a final report by the Deputy Superintendent of Police, Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau, a complaint case was initiated.
During the trial, the prosecution examined 45 witnesses and marked 130 exhibits, while the appellant examined himself as a defence witness.
The Special Judge convicted him in 2009 and sentenced him to two years' rigorous imprisonment with a fine of Rs 5,50,000.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday referred the long-running dispute between Reliance Industries Limited and the Government of India concerning the exploration and extraction of natural gas in the Krishna-Godavari (KG) basin to mediation.
The bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Baghchi and Justice V Mohana requested former Supreme Court judge Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai to act as the mediator.
It also requested her to take the assistance of two domain experts, to be suggested by the parties.
The Court noted that both sides had sought adjournments from time to time to explore the possibility of a settlement but had been unable to arrive at a viable solution.
Attorney General for India R Venkataramani and Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal informed the bench that the discussions did not reach a resolution.
"Both sides have requested adjournment from time to time to enable the parties to explore settlement.
We are informed that they themselves have not been able to find out a viable solution," the Court observed.
"In view of the request made on their behalf, we request Justice Ranjana P. Desai to act as the mediator.
We also request her to have the assistance of two domain experts as may be suggested by the parties," it added.

The dispute concerns allegations that Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) extracted natural gas that had migrated from an adjoining block operated by the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) into its own block in the Krishna-Godavari (KG) basin.
ONGC alleged that the gas reservoirs in the two blocks were interconnected, resulting in the migration of gas from its block into RIL's block.

Following a study by DeGolyer and MacNaughton, which indicated connectivity between the reservoirs, the Union Government constituted a committee headed by former Supreme Court judge Justice AP Shah to examine the issue.

stories.headline: SC turns down NIA plea challenging Khurram Parvez's bail
stories.title: SC turns down NIA plea challenging Khurram Parvez's bail
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 30 : The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed a plea filed by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) challenging the Delhi High Court's decision to grant bail to Kashmiri human rights activist Khurram Parvez in a terror conspiracy case. A bench of Justices M.M. Sundresh and P.B. Varale declined to interfere with the High Court's order granting relief to Parvez, who has been in custody for nearly five years. Senior advocate Tanveer Ahmed Mir, appearing for Parvez, submitted before the apex court that his client has a prosthetic leg and has already undergone incarceration of almost five years. He further informed the Justice Sundresh-led Bench that the framing of charges in the case had been deferred after the NIA sought time to file a supplementary chargesheet. The NIA had approached the Supreme Court challenging the Delhi High Court's June 10 order granting bail to Parvez in the case registered under the stringent provisions of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). Parvez has been in custody since November 2021 in connection with the alleged larger conspiracy linked to Pakistan-based terror outfit Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT). The NIA has accused him of being involved in terror funding, recruitment of overground workers, collecting sensitive information concerning security forces and promoting separatist activities in Jammu and Kashmir. The Delhi High Court, while granting bail, had observed that Parvez's prolonged incarceration of over four and a half years and the unlikelihood of the trial concluding in the near future warranted his release despite the stringent restrictions under the UAPA. A division bench of Justices Navin Chawla and Ravinder Dudeja had set aside the trial court's December 13, 2024, order rejecting his bail plea. It had taken into account that the trial was still at the stage of arguments on framing of charges and that the prosecution intended to examine 197 witnesses if charges were framed. It had observed that the right to personal liberty under Article 21 of the Constitution had to be balanced against the restrictions imposed under Section 43D(5) of the UAPA. "The appellant's rights under Article 21 of the Constitution of India need to be balanced and may even trump the restriction imposed under Section 43D(5) of the UAPA," the Justice Chawla-led Bench had said. The High Court had also considered Parvez's physical infirmity, noting that he had lost a leg in a landmine blast in 2004. The prosecution case against him was also primarily based on the statement of co-accused Muneer Ahmad Kataria, who subsequently turned approver, the High Court had recorded. It observed that the allegations made through the approver's statement were yet to be tested during the trial and refrained from expressing any opinion on the merits of the case. While granting relief, the High Court had imposed stringent conditions, including furnishing a personal bond of Rs 2 lakh with two sureties, surrendering his passport, restricting his movements outside Delhi without permission and reporting periodically to the investigating officer. It had also directed Parvez not to influence witnesses, comment publicly on the merits of the case or engage in any activity prejudicial to public order or the integrity of the trial. --IANS
